points: **Matrix** disease changes the nail plate: pits, ridges, Beau’s lines, leukonychia.
**Nail-bed** disease changes how the plate attaches and its colour: onycholysis, oil-drop patches, splinter haemorrhages, subungual thickening.
**Clubbing** reflects soft-tissue overgrowth of the fingertip, thought to be driven by platelet-derived growth factors bypassing the lung capillaries.
Look at **all 20 nails**, the skin, scalp and joints.
Ask about recent illness, chemotherapy, new drugs, trauma, wet work and nail cosmetics.
Send clippings if fungal infection is possible, because psoriasis and onychomycosis can look identical and can coexist.
For clubbing, check Schamroth’s window (lost diamond-shaped gap when the backs of two fingertips are pressed together) and look for chest, cardiac, liver or bowel signs.

items.t: **New clubbing**: same-week GP review for chest, cardiac, liver or bowel causes; chest X-ray is often the first test.
Nail psoriasis with joint pain or dactylitis: screen for **psoriatic arthritis** (PEST) and refer to rheumatology.

pearls.t: Dating a Beau’s line: fingernails grow about 3 mm a month, so a line 6 mm from the cuticle marks an event about 2 months ago.
Nail psoriasis predicts psoriatic arthritis: ask about joint pain and morning stiffness at every review.
Treat nail psoriasis expectations carefully: improvement takes months, and topical treatment works best on the nail folds.
